sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Lesson 2.3 of Dataset Fundamentals: Acquisition Instruments—Surveys, Observational Protocols, and Web Scraping. In modern data systems, raw data does not simply exist waiting to be consumed. It must be acquired through structured observation.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: We face two distinct operational paradigms: Active Structured Inquiry, where we probe respondents through psychometric surveys, and Passive Automated Extraction, where we harvest information from Document Object Models across the web. Both paradigms introduce unique failure modes: non-response attrition bias in surveys, and structural drift and rate-limiting throttling in web scraping. In this masterclass, we will formalize the mathematics of Inverse Propensity Weighting, derive Little's law of politeness and crawl-delay engineering, and build resilient collection pipelines.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Slide 2 maps the end-to-end taxonomy of data acquisition instruments. In the Active Protocol branch on the left, we formulate psychometric survey designs—Likert items, categorical choices, and branching logic. However, non-response attrition inevitably occurs, requiring inverse propensity weighting to model the response probability pi and restore population balance.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: On the right, the Passive Protocol branch begins with an audit of the target host's RFC 9309 robots.txt file to respect crawl delays and permissions, followed by DOM tree parsing with robust semantic selectors, and structural drift monitoring. Notice how both branches converge toward rigorous data quality guarantees.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: In survey methodology, Groves and colleagues formalized how non-response distorts empirical estimates. Let the true population mean Y bar be partitioned between respondents r and non-respondents nr. If f sub r represents the observed response rate, the true mean equals f sub r times Y bar sub r plus 1 minus f sub r times Y bar sub nr.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Subtracting the true mean from the respondent mean reveals the non-response bias formula: Bias of y bar sub r equals 1 minus f sub r times the difference between Y bar sub r and Y bar sub nr. Notice the profound insight here: non-response bias does not depend solely on a low response rate. Even with a ninety percent response rate, if the ten percent non-respondents are drastically different, severe bias still contaminates the study.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: To eliminate non-response bias, survey statisticians leverage auxiliary covariates X sub i that are observed for both respondents and non-respondents—such as demographic census data or platform usage telemetry. We model the response propensity pi sub i, defined as the probability that response indicator R sub i equals one given X sub i, typically using logistic regression.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Each respondent is then assigned an inverse propensity weight w sub i equal to 1 over pi sub i. By the classical Horvitz-Thompson theorem from 1952, weighting each respondent by the inverse of their inclusion probability yields an unbiased estimate of the population mean, provided the Missing at Random condition holds.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: While Inverse Propensity Weighting achieves asymptotic unbiasedness, it introduces severe variance instability when propensity scores approach zero. A respondent with pi sub i equal to 0.005 receives a weight of 200, causing a single outlier to dominate the entire estimator.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: In production dataset collection, engineers enforce weight trimming or propensity clipping, bounding estimated propensities between alpha and 1 minus alpha—typically 0.05 and 0.95. Furthermore, we monitor the Kish effective sample size to track how much statistical power is lost to weight variance. When non-response is Non-Ignorable—meaning Missing Not at Random—IPW fails, and researchers must deploy Heckman two-step selection models to estimate the latent selection hazard lambda.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Survey Non-Response and IPW Debiasing Workbench! Here, our stage has docked directly above the interactive simulation controls. Adjust the Response Rate slider between ten percent and ninety percent. Observe how the unweighted respondent mean diverges from the true population mean whenever the latent gap between respondents and non-respondents widens. Notice how the IPW Horvitz-Thompson estimator reconstructs the population target.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Time for our first active checkpoint. Consider this real-world scenario: A customer satisfaction survey is sent to ten thousand users, achieving an observed response rate of twenty percent. The respondent mean score is 8.5 out of 10. A rigorous telephone follow-up audit of non-respondents reveals their true satisfaction score is only 4.5 out of 10. Calculate the exact true overall customer satisfaction Y bar, and determine the magnitude of non-response bias. Select Option A, B, or C above me.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Now we transition from active inquiry to passive automated extraction: web scraping. In production data engineering, a web scraper is not a script that blindly hammers URLs. It is a distributed network client governed by RFC 9309, the Robots Exclusion Protocol. The target site publishes a robots.txt file that dictates allowed paths, disallowed directories, and crawl delays.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: The fundamental rule of scraping politeness dictates that the inter-request delay T delay must be at least the maximum of the specified crawl delay and the reciprocal of the server's maximum rate limit. Furthermore, ethical scrapers identify themselves via a transparent User-Agent string containing contact information, cache previously fetched responses, and implement exponential backoff on HTTP 429 and 503 errors.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: An HTML document is fundamentally an ordered tree T equals V comma E, where vertices represent HTML tags and edges represent parent-child nesting. Parsing this document tree has a computational complexity of O of V plus E. When junior engineers write scrapers, they often copy absolute XPath expressions directly from browser developer tools—such as slash html slash body slash div 2 slash table slash tr 3 slash td 1.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: These absolute positional selectors are catastrophic in production. The moment the site adds a banner advertisement or a top navigation bar, the entire path breaks and yields empty values. Production data collectors use semantic invariant predicates that target unique attributes, data test IDs, and semantic classes.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Even with semantic selectors, target websites eventually undergo complete architectural migrations—such as transitioning from server-rendered HTML to client-side Single Page Applications. To detect this before millions of corrupted records enter downstream pipelines, production scrapers track the structural fingerprint of the DOM using Jaccard distance.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: We extract the set S sub t of HTML structural tags and class tokens for each page. The Jaccard distance between the current DOM fingerprint and the baseline fingerprint is one minus the size of the intersection divided by the size of the union. When this metric crosses a threshold—typically 0.35—the scraper triggers an automated circuit breaker and alerts engineers.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Slide 11 illustrates the end-to-end architecture of a production-grade web crawling system. At the top, target seeds are managed by a distributed URL Frontier Queue, backed by Redis or Kafka, enforcing per-domain domain-level politeness. Before any request fires, the RFC 9309 Gatekeeper checks robots.txt cached rules and ensures the token bucket rate limiter does not exceed maximum allowable requests per second.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: The worker determines whether the target requires headless browser execution using Playwright for JavaScript hydration, or lightweight HTTP parsing using lxml. Extracted records undergo structural drift verification and MinHash deduplication before persisting to raw data lakes, while malformed payloads are routed to a Dead-Letter Queue.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to our second interactive lab: The Web Scraping Rate Limiter and Structural Drift Simulator. Our speaker dock is now positioned above the simulator controls. Try setting Crawl Delay to 0.5 seconds and observe how the maximum allowable rate is calculated as 2.0 requests per second. If you increase the concurrent worker count beyond this threshold, watch our safety badge transition into a critical Denial of Service violation. Then, adjust the DOM Tag Mutation Rate slider to simulate target redesigns—watch the Jaccard distance metric climb until it trips the automated circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let us test your engineering intuition on scraping throughput. A remote website publishes a robots.txt file containing the directive Crawl-delay: 0.5. What is the absolute maximum request rate per second an ethical automated scraper can issue against this host across all concurrent worker threads? Select Option A, B, or C above me.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Slide 14 reviews a landmark empirical case study in multi-modal collection: The Nordic PharmacoEpidemiological Network, or NorPEN, medication adherence study. Researchers initially dispatched mailed surveys across Scandinavian cohorts. The survey suffered a dismal twenty-one percent response rate. More alarmingly, demographic audits revealed that healthy, affluent patients responded at 3.2 times the rate of chronically ill or low-income patients, introducing massive healthy-user confounding bias.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: To overcome this, researchers augmented the study by scraping 1.2 million open clinical registry update records from Nordic healthcare portals. Finally, by calibrating Horvitz-Thompson IPW weights against national census auxiliary data, researchers eliminated ninety-four percent of the healthy-user bias.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Slide 15 provides production Python code implementing survey Inverse Propensity Weighting. The function compute_ipw_survey_estimate takes a pandas DataFrame, fits a logistic regression model on observable covariates X to predict response probability, clips propensities between 0.05 and 0.95 to protect against extreme weight inflation, and computes the Horvitz-Thompson weighted mean.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: In the execution benchmark below, five thousand synthetic records are generated where older individuals respond at significantly higher rates. The unweighted respondent mean overestimates true population income by thousands of dollars. The IPW correction successfully eliminates over eighty percent of this non-response bias, validated by automated assertions.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: To conclude Lesson 2.3, let us synthesize the Four Golden Rules of Acquisition Instruments. First, never assume survey non-response is ignorable. Always capture auxiliary covariates and deploy Inverse Propensity Weighting under Missing at Random assumptions. Second, always stabilize your weights. Clip propensities and monitor effective sample sizes to prevent variance explosion.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Third, in web scraping, strictly obey RFC 9309 robots.txt directives and compute hard concurrency limits based on crawl delays. Fourth, never rely on absolute positional DOM paths. Use semantic invariant predicates and monitor Jaccard structural drift to catch upstream UI redesigns. In Lesson 2.4, we will expand from web scraping to APIs—exploring REST, GraphQL, and streaming webhooks.
